Article Title: FPCE writes to PM Modi, lists 5 key changes to RERA to strengthen homebuyer protection
Article Text:
FPCE writes to PM calling for separating promotion and development of the real estate sector.

The organisation has made five key recommendations:

Separate real estate development from homebuyer protection: Keep the promotion and development of the real estate sector separate from the law designed to protect homebuyers. Re-enact RERA: Bring in a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act that places the interests of homebuyers at its centre. Shift administration to a consumer protection ministry: Entrust the law's administration to a ministry whose primary mandate is consumer protection, such as the Department of Consumer Affairs. Ensure accountability: Introduce an effective accountability framework for real estate regulatory authorities . Prepare a time-bound action plan: Direct the ministry of housing and urban affairs to examine FPCE's report and draw up an action plan with clear timelines.

NEW DELHI: The Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE), which spearheaded the movement for the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking changes to the law to strengthen homebuyer protection.In its letter, FPCE has called for separating the promotion and development of the real estate sector from the legal framework meant to protect homebuyers.It has also sought the re-enactment of RERA as a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act, with consumer protection at its core.
Article Summary: The Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It has called for separating the promotion and development of the real estate sector from the legal framework meant to protect homebuyers. The group has also sought the re-enactment of RERA as a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh government on Monday informed the Supreme Court that a chargesheet has been filed in the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple in Ayodhya, with the court permitting the petitioners to assist the local magistrate during the trial.A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant disposed of the petitions concerning the alleged theft of temple donations and directed the judicial magistrate to proceed with the case in accordance with the law.The Supreme Court also clarified that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the allegations.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, informed the court that the alleged theft took place during the counting of donations at the temple. Article Title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
Article Text:
IT professional and wife face Rs 5.3 crore taxevasion allegations over fabricated donation and loan claims, including forged documents and receipts. (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to those making false income tax claims, authorities have carried out a rare search action on an IT professional and his wife, estimating alleged bogus claims and tax evasion of Rs 5.3 crore over five years, according to the department. The couple also face charges of forging documents.Tax officials found that deduction claims involved fake political donations, interest on home and education loans, while rental income was not disclosed. They had purchased half-a-dozen properties using some of these funds.It all started with the wife's tax return claiming a deduction of over Rs 40 lakh for a donation to a political party. While her Form 16 showed deductions of around Rs 1.2 lakh, the return claimed an additional deduction. When the claim was verified with the party, officials found that the taxpayer had actually donated Rs 50, for which a receipt had been issued. Investigators found that the receipt had been digitally modified and several fabricated receipts generated to support the claim of a donation exceeding Rs 40 lakh.But the couple, who live in Delhi-NCR, did not give in easily. When summoned during the investigation, the husband, who filed the returns, not only presented the "modified" receipts but also submitted bank statements to support the claim.Officials sought to verify the statements with the bank, as the transactions did not tally.Loan payments, credit card payments and bank transfers, including transfers to their own account, had been forged to show them as political donations.The couple had claimed nearly Rs 3 crore in education loan interest for studies at Yale University. An interest certificate was submitted. During probe, officials discovered that no family member of the couple under scrutiny had ever studied at Yale and that the certificate had been prepared using ChatGPT.The couple also made a bogus housing loan claim, with both spouses describing themselves as the sole owner of the same property, although they have now admitted that it was jointly owned. Contrary to their claims, the property was always rented out and was not self-occupied.In their returns, one spouse had claimed nil rental income and interest payment of Rs 2 lakh, while the other had claimed up to Rs 5 lakh as interest income. Since tax returns now require individuals to disclose loan account number and the bank, the name of the bank was changed in one case and the loan amount increased to Rs 6 crore, with interest claimed at Rs 8 lakh. The probe revealed that the loan had been repaid in 2015, while the claims under scrutiny related to the period beginning FY2021-22. The property was earning rent of Rs 10-16 lakh during this period.Dealing with the couple has not been easy. When their case was first picked up, the husband shifted the deduction claim for political donations under Section 80GGC to donations to charities under Section 80G, without surrendering the claim.The couple now face penalties and other legal action.
Article Summary: IT professional and wife face Rs 5.3 crore taxevasion allegations over fabricated donation and loan claims, including forged documents and receipts. The couple, who live in Delhi-NCR, did not give in easily. The husband, who filed the returns, not only presented the "modified" receipts but also submitted bank statements to support the claim.

Article Title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant calls for more transparent and predictable case listings, stressing that timely court intervention can make the difference between justice and injustice.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Flagging the importance of timely intervention by courts in crucial matters, CJI Surya Kant said the difference between justice and injustice was not in the final judgement but in whether the court intervened when "intervention was most needed".He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working and to make listing of cases "more transparent and predictable".Speaking at the platinum jubilee celebration of Kerala HC, CJI Kant said constitutional justice in India did not begin and end in New Delhi and its strength lay in the robust network of 25 HCs spread across the country, each entrusted with the duty of protecting rights and upholding the rule of law.He said HCs were better placed to deal with citizens' problems as they were closely connected with the everyday realities of people."It is in this context that I wish to emphasise the extraordinary constitutional significance of Article 226. Its breadth is one of the greatest strengths of our judicial architecture. While Article 32 guarantees access to SC for enforcement of fundamental rights, Article 226 empowers HCs to issue appropriate writs and directions not only for fundamental rights but also for other legal rights.This wide constitutional canvas allows HCs to fashion meaningful remedies across diverse legal, statutory, administrative and contractual disputes. Equally important is their power to grant timely interim protection," the CJI said.He said there has been a growing tendency of litigants to approach SC requesting directions for urgent listing or early hearing of matters pending before HCs and asked whether the present process could be improved, including listing of cases."SC has consistently respected the institutional autonomy of HCs, including their authority to regulate their own rosters. That position is rooted in respect for the constitutional status of these institutions. Yet, the frequency of such requests invites us to consider whether there is room to improve the responsiveness of our processes. We must ask ourselves: Can urgent matters be identified more effectively? Can listing procedures be made more transparent and predictable? Can technology assist in prioritising cases where delay may cause irreversible prejudice?. .." he said."These are not questions of institutional criticism but of collective responsibility," the CJI added.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant calls for more transparent and predictable case listings. He says timely court intervention can make the difference between justice and injustice. He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working.

Article Text:
Airlines have been asked to give a break-up of tariff in terms of the total amount payable by a passenger and break-up of the same by displaying components like base fare, tax, fees, cancellation charges, refund conditions and any other charge separately.

NEW DELHI: India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest. ” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extraordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.“Every air transport undertaking… shall establish tariff based on factors including cost of operation…. (They) shall submit tariff to the Director General (DGCA) in such form, manner and periodicity as may be specified…. (They) shall publish tariff on their websites… for wider public awareness and transparency,” says the gazette notification published Saturday (October 31).Airlines have been asked to give a break-up of tariff in terms of the total amount payable by a passenger and break-up of the same by displaying components like base fare, tax, fees, cancellation charges, refund conditions and any other charge separately.Regarding intervention in “extraordinary circumstances,” it says: “Where the central government is of the opinion that (in) an extraordinary situation it may, by order in writing, issue such directions in public interest…. such directions shall be proportionate to the circumstances and shall remain in force for the period specified only.”
Article Summary: Airlines have been asked to give a break-up of tariff in terms of the total amount payable by a passenger. Government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest.

Article Title: Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
Article Text:
Cash doesn't cross Myanmar border, payments made in kind: ED

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: International illicit drug syndicates operating out of the Golden Triangle of Myanmar, Thailand and Laos have turned to age-old barter trade, under which drugs like heroin and methamphetamine are smuggled into India through the porous borders of Northeastern states and payments are made in kind through supplies of petrol, diesel, flour, edible oil, groceries, medicines, footwear and clothing from their Indian network.Drug lords across border ensure transactions are made without any money actually crossing border, according to an investigation report compiled by the ED after week-long searches at 38 locations across the Northeast last week.Myanmar has already replaced Afghanistan as world's largest illicit opium-producing region. With precursor chemicals moved from India to Myanmar, where drug manufacturing units are located, finished heroin, brown sugar and synthetic drug methamphetamine tablets are produced and carried across the Tiau river at Zokhawthar, the border crossing opposite Khawmawi in Myanmar. Consignments are staged at Champhai, from where they travel down the Champhai-Aizawl road and NH-06A to Aizawl, Vairengte and then to Assam and the rest of India, the ED report said.ED has traced intermediaries who procured and supplied goods to syndicates in Myanmar. Over 1,400 mule bank accounts, mostly belonging to traders who procured these goods and supplied them to the network, have been frozen. Transactions involving goods worth over Rs 270 crore have been identified so far and six persons arrested.These transactions were handled by illicit money exchangers, or hawala networks, in Champhai, including Rs 125 crore in cash received from Assam, Nagaland, WB, Tripura & Delhi, ED said.Significantly, drug money reaching hawala accounts in Aizawl and Champhai came substantially from Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai, ED added. Illegal money is converted into ordinary, commercially marketable goods, which are sent to border towns of Mizoram and onward to Myanmar."The banking system is thus used only for Indian leg of the transaction, where the payment looks like an ordinary trade payment backed by a GST invoice. The cross-border leg moves as goods and leaves no money trail. In effect, fuel, flour and groceries have become currency in which Myanmar-based drug suppliers are paid," ED said.The probe is in progress to identify consignees in border towns, those who move goods across border, Myanmar-based recipients, petrol pumps, shops and suppliers paid in the same manner, and money exchangers directing the accounts. ED is also tracing and attaching further proceeds of crime as it works to dismantle the financial networks sustaining narcotics trafficking.
Article Summary: Myanmar has already replaced Afghanistan as world's largest illicit opium- producing region. With precursor chemicals moved from India to Myanmar, finished heroin, brown sugar and synthetic drug methamphetamine tablets are produced. Transactions involving goods worth over Rs 270 crore have been identified so far and six persons arrested.

Article Title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi cites World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate fell 90% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023, with nearly 50 crore people lifted out of extreme poverty.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has recorded one of the fastest poverty declines in the world, with the extreme poverty rate in the country "collapsing" by 90% between 2011 and 2023 to a low of 2.6%, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday, while asserting that elimination of poverty is a commitment for his govt."A historic fall in poverty. A generational rise in opportunity... Gareebi hatao was never a slogan for us. It is our commitment. From more than 1 in 4 Indians to roughly 1 in 38 (in extreme poverty)," the PM posted on Instagram Saturday, citing the World Bank's latest numbers. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years.Besides, Modi added, employment had grown by 13.4 crore between 2017 and 2023, which was nearly twice the increase in India's working age population. "Inequality has fallen sharply. India's Gini index has dropped by over 20% from 29 in 2011 to 23 in 2023," the Prime Minister said in the Instagram post. The Gini index reflects how equitable is the distribution of income or wealth across a population, with a lower number indicating greater equality.World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028 from 57.7% in 2011, having fallen to 16.1% in 2023.Meanwhile, extreme poverty, defined as spending $3 a day, declined from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023."This progress was mainly driven by strong consumption growth; rising employment, especially among women; and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited access to stable employment and higher dependency ratios. Wage disparities, however, remain pronounced, as median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023," the World Bank had said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi cites World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate fell 90% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years. World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028.

Article Title: Nita Ambani marks birthday with foundation stone ceremony for 5,000-person care facility
Article Text: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra. The project, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, is envisioned as a lifelong home for more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and people with developmental disabilities.Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township, being established by Reliance Foundation, will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.Nita Ambani said the project was a step towards creating “a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort”. She said the township would combine medical support with the warmth of family life and give residents opportunities to learn, work, make friends and participate in festivals and celebrations.According to the plans shared by Reliance Foundation, the township will support a wider community of approximately 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.The proposed facility will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India. Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by house parents and caregivers. Their rooms will be designed to offer familiarity and personal belonging, with residents encouraged to personalise their living spaces.The project will include a specialised hospital offering developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry, palliative care and other medical services. Rehabilitation facilities for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy are also planned.Other proposed amenities include a temple, gardens, farms, playgrounds, workshops, cafés and inclusive sports and recreational facilities. An animal companionship farm is expected to be developed with expertise from Vantara.The township will also offer vocational training and employment opportunities through facilities such as a bakery, café and craft studios. A dedicated training academy for disability-care professionals, a hospice wing and a garden of remembrance are also part of the plans.The initiative is expected to have an impact beyond the township. Around 1,000 people from nearby areas are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, while respite-care facilities, mobile medical clinics and outreach programmes will support families in neighbouring districts.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.

Article Title: Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
Article Text:
The arrests come days after singer Diljit Dosanjh performed in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Three people, including a woman, have been arrested for allegedly writing pro-Khalistan slogans at two Delhi Metro stations, police said on Sunday. The graffiti also carried a message targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh.The arrests come days after Dosanjh performed in the national capital on Friday as part of his Aura India Tour. The singer is scheduled to take the tour to several other cities over the next two months.The graffiti was found at Jahangirpuri and Shastri Nagar Metro stations on October 29 and 30, respectively. Police said the accused were allegedly promised substantial financial rewards for defacing public property at prominent locations in Delhi.The arrested persons have been identified as Sumeet alias Raftar (30), a resident of Panipat in Haryana, and Sumit Kumar alias Kaka (22) and Gurpreet (22), both from Punjab.According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Narra Chaitanya, the investigation revealed that Sumit Kumar was allegedly the main instigator.Sumeet allegedly painted the slogans near Gate No. 1 of Jahangirpuri Metro station and recorded a video of the act to send to his handlers.Kumar and Gurpreet allegedly defaced a staircase wall near Gate No. 2 of Shastri Nagar Metro station."In both instances, the graffiti read "Diljit Singh quam d gaddar khoon d badla SFJ Khalistan", expressing support for the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) and Khalistan ideology. These acts defaced public property in Metro stations and posed a threat to public order and national integrity," the police said, ANI reported.Police said Sumit Kumar had been in contact with SFJ sympathisers in Ludhiana and Gurdaspur before an associate allegedly instructed him to download an encrypted messaging application.A member linked to the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) allegedly shared graffiti templates through the app and offered him financial rewards for carrying out the activity at prominent Metro stations.Kumar then allegedly recruited Gurpreet and Sumeet to execute the plan. The three travelled to Delhi on October 28, police said.Police said Sumeet ad come in contact with Kumar through online platforms and had visited Ludhiana about a week before the incident. The trio travelled to Delhi by taxi and reached ISBT Kashmere Gate on October 29.Investigators also found that Kumar and Gurpreet had known each other for around four years. Kumar allegedly persuaded her to travel to Delhi on the pretext of shopping before informing her about the plan, police said.Police further alleged that Kumar had painted graffiti near the GTK Bypass, under the jurisdiction of Samaypur Badli police station, on October 30. That incident is being investigated separately.Two FIRs were registered at the Metro Azadpur and Metro NSP police stations under Section 3 of the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Public Property Act, 2007, and Section 62(2) of the Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002."Further investigation is underway to identify other persons involved in the network and establish the role of the handlers behind the alleged operation," the officer said.
Article Summary: The arrests come days after singer Diljit Dosanjh performed in New Delhi. The graffiti was found at Jahangirpuri and Shastri Nagar Metro stations. Police said the accused were allegedly promised substantial financial rewards for defacing public property.

Article Title: Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
Article Text:
Union minister Kiren Rijiju during a meeting with Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck during his visit to Gelephu, Bhutan (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, recognising his contribution to strengthening friendship between the two countries. The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City on Sunday.According to news agency ANI, Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture, describing it as a "huge honour for India". He also conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the Bhutanese King.In a post on X, Rijiju said, "It's a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens."He further said, "Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H E Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan.A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations."Stupas are sacred Buddhist structures associated with the teachings and life of Gautama Buddha. Traditionally, they were built to preserve the relics of the Buddha and other revered Buddhist figures, including their ashes and remains. Over time, they became important places of worship, meditation and religious devotion.The 108 stupas in Bhutan are known as Jangchub Chortens, or Stupas of Enlightenment. The number 108 holds special significance in Buddhist traditions and is associated with religious practices, including the use of 108 beads in prayer malas. The structures are intended to promote peace, harmony and spiritual well-being.Rijiju is visiting Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. Earlier on Sunday, Rijiju met Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu. The two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.
Article Summary: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture.

Article Title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption

NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.“Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups—comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)—about 80% of these shops—roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000—remained closed today,” he said.Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.“The movement of goods—loading and unloading—was completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,” he said.Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.“The question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for it—will the organisers do so?” he said.He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.Ahead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue."We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asia’s largest commercial zone—with major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.Amid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.“I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,” he said, adding, “But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.”The INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.
Article Summary: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday. Traders claim losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.

Article Title: Desi Bullet Train closer to reality as squeeze test nears completion
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for final production of the country’s first indigenous Bullet Train, B28, the “Squeeze Test” or vehicle body shell test of the first coach is underway and will be completed next week. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML’s Bengaluru facility on Sunday.A squeeze test is a safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure in case of a collision or crash. “Squeeze test of the integrated car body is at final stage. After this, propulsion system will be placed and all electronic systems will be put in place. Subsequently, a climatic test will be carried out wherein the car will be subjected to tests at high temperature of 50 degree Celsius and negative temperature, and dusty and heavy rain environment conditions,” Vaishnaw said.Railways plans to start the test run of the high-speed train, designed to operate at a maximum speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph, from first quarter of 2027-2028 on Surat-Vapi (100 km) section of Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed corridor.The commercial run is scheduled for August 2027. Each bullet train will have eight coaches and another eight can be added later. The eight-car train can carry 557 passengers.BEML, a central PSU, is manufacturing the first two of the indigenous bullet trains, each comprising eight coaches.“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official said.While seeking Cabinet approval for the escalated cost of the country’s first bullet train project, the railway ministry had stated that two prototype trains were expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. It had also said that the entire Gujarat section of the corridor was expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by December 2030.
Article Summary: The squeeze test is a safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML's Bengaluru facility on Sunday.

Article Title: SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Article Text:
SC allows tax department to reopen assessment of former CJI YK Sabharwal's sons over Rs 255 crore share sale deals.

2015 notice of assessing officer issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that the income tax department is not precluded from conducting reassessment upon discovering evidence suggesting income had escaped assessment, Supreme Court upheld a Delhi high court order allowing the agency to reassess the income of the sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal for 2008-09 and 2009-10.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the Sabharwals' appeal and said the notice issued by the department in 2015 was valid as it was based on reasons duly recorded and on tangible material of a report of its investigation unit.Recording details of financial transactions, the Supreme Court bench noted Chetan Sabharwal along with his brother Nitin Sabharwal and two other shareholders entered into two share purchase agreements with GYS Real Estate Pvt Ltd (buyer company) for a sale of 7.5 lakh equity shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and 2.5 lakh equity shares of SVIIT Software (P) Ltd held by each of the parties for a sale consideration of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively. The appellant and other selling shareholders were each entitled to 1/4th share of the total consideration. "We are of the firm view that the impugned notice dated March 31, 2015, issued by the assessing officer under Section 148 of Income Tax Act, for initiating reassessment for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10, was issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid," the bench said."The reasons rest on tangible material, namely the report of the DGIT Investigation Unit, Noida, which concluded that shares of company No.1 (Pawan Impex (P) Ltd) and company No. 2 (SVIIT Software (P) Ltd) were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, and they have a rational nexus and a live link with the belief formed by the assessing officer," it said.Subsequent to completion of assessment, the investigation unit conducted enquiries into the value of the shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd and prepared a report. The report concluded, prima facie, that the shares were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, which was much lower than the transaction amounts of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively.The enquiries revealed the appellants purchased one-half share of the property at Sikandara Road, Delhi, in April 2010 through a court auction, and that the major source of this investment was the sale proceeds of the shares of the companies. On perusal of the investigation report and after a gap of four years, the department issued a notice under Section 148 of the act for reassessment.
Article Summary: Supreme Court upheld a Delhi high court order allowing the agency to reassess the income of the sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal for 2008-09 and 2009-10. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the Sabharwals' appeal.

New Delhi: Public sector Coal India Limited (CIL) recorded its highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 million tonnes (MT), registering a robust 19% growth over the 59.2 MT supplied during the corresponding period in FY26, despite operational challenges posed by unseasonal rainfall, Puja festivities and the impact of a cyclone, amid rising power demand.The previous monthly record of 69.4 MT was achieved in March 2026, CIL said in a statement. Article Title: International Digi Yatra trials to begin at 7 airports for Indian nationals this year for wider rollout in 2027: Government
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra (DY). India will hold trials for international passengers at seven airports in the three months of this year, allowing eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use DY at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.The aviation ministry said trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. “Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, security hold areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027,” it said in a statement.To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based “verifiable credential” (VC) through DY mobile application. “The process involves scanning the machine readable zone (MRZ) of e-passport, reading the embedded chip using the near field communication (NFC) feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passenger’s Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials,” the statement said.The facility will complement, and not replace, existing travel processes. “Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities,” it added.IndiGo said eligible passengers can upload their boarding pass to the Digi Yatra app. After completing mandatory document verification at airline check-in counter, they can proceed through the security hold area and boarding gates using DY biometric face authentication.IndiGo chief digital and information officer Neetan Chopra said: “At IndiGo, we are committed to redefining air travel by making it more seamless, efficient, and customer centric, and we believe that technology can be a key catalyst in this evolution. Having been a key part of the technical proof of concept earlier this year, we are pleased to partner with Digi Yatra for the launch of these international passenger trials. Expanding secure digital identity and biometric technologies to international departures is a significant step forward for Indian aviation. We are committed to delivering a seamless travel experience for our customers at every touchpoint. The successful deployment of this technology marks an important step in reimagining the airport experience, combining enhanced security, convenience and operational efficiency. As the aviation industry continues to evolve, such innovations will play a key role in shaping the future of passenger travel.”Digi Yatra Foundation CEO Suresh Khadakbhavi said: “Digi Yatra has demonstrated how digital identity can simplify domestic air travel. With the start of international passenger trials, we are taking an important step towards extending this experience to eligible Indian nationals travelling internationally.Interoperability with global frameworks such as IATA’s One ID and ICAO’s Public Key Directory (PKD) will be an important part of this journey, helping explore how e-passport-based digital credentials can enable more seamless and secure passenger journeys across borders, while keeping passenger consent, privacy and security central to the experience. ”Digi Yatra platform has over 2.6 crore users at present and has enabled more than 11 crore journeys across 39 domestic airports, serving domestic airlines. A further 25 domestic airports are planned to be covered by 2027. “The aviation ministry remains committed to leveraging technology to improve airport operations and facilitate seamless air travel, in line with govt's vision of Digital India and ease of flying. ”
Article Summary: India will trial Digi Yatra for international passengers at seven airports over the next three months. To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based “verifiable credential” (VC) through DY mobile application.

Article Title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
Article Text:

External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian shipping, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.According to news agency ANI, Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said India was engaging with the parties on three key aspects of the conflict, including the safety of civilian vessels and seafarers, the restoration of grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure. He said India was trying to bring the concerned parties together to address these issues."One, not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers," he said, outlining the first of the three areas discussed with Russia, Ukraine and Europe.On the second issue, Jaishankar stressed the need to restore grain shipments from both Russia and Ukraine, warning that exports through the Black Sea had declined sharply amid the conflict."The second, to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine, these are two major exporters of grain for the global markets, can be restored, because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.Jaishankar further highlighted the complexities involved in ensuring the safety of energy infrastructure, saying different parties had different interpretations of what should be covered under such an understanding."And the third is with regard to energy. Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players. There is energy infrastructure itself. To some, it would mean a refinery; to some, it would mean grids. There would be issues relating to ships carrying fuel," he said.He added that India is attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues, particularly on the protection of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments.The concerns raised by Jaishankar extend beyond the immediate conflict, given the Black Sea's importance to global trade. Any disruption to commercial shipping can affect the movement of essential commodities, raise freight and insurance costs and put pressure on international supply chains.Similarly, attacks on refineries, electricity grids and fuel-carrying vessels can disrupt energy supplies and push up global prices. Together, the safety of maritime routes, grain exports and energy infrastructure remains critical to maintaining stability in global food and energy markets.
Article Summary: India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian shipping, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure. India is attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues, particularly on the protection of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments.

NEW DELHI: Chopper operations on Char Dham routes could come to standstill from Monday. Following a chopper crashing soon after take off from Badrinath on Friday (October 30), killing all six people on board — a pilot and five passengers, the DGCA has made it mandatory for choppers operating on Char Dham to be manned by two pilots starting Monday (Nov 2), in a bid to improve safety. However chopper operators have termed the move unviable and threatened to suspend these sorties from Monday “until the matter is reviewed and a mutually workable solution is arrived at.Chopper operators on Saturday sent their “collective objection to the implementation of mandatory twin-pilot operations and intimation of suspension of operations from Nov 2, 2026,” to Directorate General of Civil Aviation chief Vir Vikram Yadav. “… (we) collectively place on record our serious concern and reservation regarding the mandatory requirement of twin-pilot operations for charter services (in) the new operational restrictions communicated by DGCA proposed to be implemented with effect from the first take-off on Nov 2, 2026. ”“The mandatory deployment of two pilots on every charter sortie will substantially increase operating costs, crew requirements, accommodation and logistical expenses, and overall operational commitments.Given the existing commercial structure, prevailing charter rates and limited operational margins, these additional costs cannot be reasonably absorbed by the operators. Nor is it commercially feasible to pass on the entire additional burden to customers,” it says.“… all operators have consistently complied with applicable DGCA regulations and have invested considerable resources in maintaining safe, efficient and reliable operations in the challenging Himalayan terrain…. any additional safety-related measures must be practical, proportionate, commercially sustainable and developed in consultation with the operating stakeholders. Accordingly, after due consideration and mutual consultation, all operators collectively express their inability to accept the mandatory twin-pilot requirement in its present form,” it says."In view of the above, we wish to formally convey that all participating operators are proposing to suspend their Char Dham charter operations with effect from Nov 2, 2026, until the matter is reviewed and a mutually workable solution is arrived at by the concerned authorities in consultation with the operators. Under the proposed framework, continuing operations would result in unsustainable financial and operational commitments, leaving the operators with no commercially viable alternative,” it said.Operators have DGCA and Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) to "reconsider the mandatory twin-pilot requirement, engage with all stakeholders on an urgent basis, and explore an alternative operational framework that adequately addresses safety concerns while ensuring the commercial viability and sustainability of helicopter operations in the region. We remain committed to aviation safety, regulatory compliance and the continued development of helicopter services in Uttarakhand. We hope that the matter will receive urgent consideration and that a constructive resolution can be reached before the proposed implementation date.”
Article Summary: Chopper operators on Char Dham routes have threatened to suspend operations from Monday over DGCA's mandatory twin-pilot rule. They cite unviable costs, after a crash killed six people. The voice of the people will triumph,” he added.Backing the rally, Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan told ANI that the demonstration could become “historic” if the government allowed it to proceed without interference. The former MP said the mobilisation was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democratic values.“If the government doesn’t interfere and allows the rally to take place, it is set to be a historic one. This rally is about saving the nation, protecting the Constitution, and safeguarding our democracy,” Hasan said.He also expressed concern over what he described as a decline in the global perception of India's electoral integrity, claiming that the country was increasingly being viewed as a “pseudo-democracy”.“The message currently circulating globally is that the world’s largest democracy has effectively become a 'pseudo-democracy', a place where votes are stolen, fair elections do not occur, and the principle of 'might is right' prevails,” he said.Hasan urged citizens to support the opposition's initiative, saying it was the duty of every Indian to stand up for the country and protect democracy.The remarks came as supporters of INDIA bloc parties began gathering at Ramlila Maidan and other locations in Delhi on Sunday morning for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally against alleged electoral irregularities.The opposition alliance is also demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress supporters assembled outside Himachal Bhawan, while Samajwadi Party workers gathered near party chief Akhilesh Yadav's residence before proceeding towards the rally venue.Party workers from several states had also reached the capital on Saturday or earlier.The march is scheduled to begin at noon from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and culminate at Ramlila Maidan.Senior opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi , Mallikarjun Kharge, Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Hemant Soren, Revanth Reddy, Tejashwi Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, are expected to attend.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had urged people travelling to Delhi for the protest to also shop from local traders ahead of Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj. In a video message posted on X on Saturday, he said the opposition's programme would not hurt businesses and asked supporters to combine their participation in the rally with some shopping.The INDIA bloc has estimated that up to 10 lakh people could attend the mobilisation, while Delhi Police expects a turnout of around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but the estimated capacity is lower — around 30,000 to 40,000 — with chairs, enclosures and passageways in place.More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, are being deployed for security and crowd management. The ground has been divided into 14 zones, with each supervised by an assistant commissioner-rank officer. More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will also be used for surveillance.The Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions and diversions in parts of central Delhi from 10 am to 5 pm on Sunday and advised commuters to plan their journeys accordingly, ANI reported.The mobilisation follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Kharge's residence on Saturday. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, during which Kharge moved a resolution listing the Opposition's charges against the CEC.Rahul Gandhi delivered the concluding remarks before the resolution was adopted.The INDIA bloc has been protesting against what it calls 'vote chori', alleging large-scale deletion of voters' names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut calls Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah the country's "only two traders" Raut says any losses suffered by the two leaders as a result of the demonstration would be acceptable. Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan says the demonstration could become 'historic' if the government allows it to proceed without interference.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
